note:
The seventeen categorical key traits per race, plus the sparse per-people delta. Everything else in heritage is derived from this file. Carried whole from heritage/policies/traits.json.

READ BY: heritage/policy.py lint_traits(); heritage/derive.py _resolve() (races[parent] as the base, peoples.get(civ_id, {}) as the delta, merged by merge_traits()), derive_culture(), derive_genome(); heritage/phonemes.py inventory(), which gates the phoneme alphabet on the six soma axes. DOWNSTREAM: icarus_sim/terrain_ruins.py:32 culture_schools() resolves every civilization's `magic_school` through this file and feeds it into the city-fate lottery -- that call replaced a hand-written twelve-row dict here and a second, unsynchronised copy in Core/legacy.cpp, so this file is now the single source for it; icarus_sim/terrain_civilizations.py:14 heritage_of() publishes the resolved traits into the world document.

RNG INPUT: indirectly -- these values select the phoneme inventory and the derivation branches that the name draws then run on. No list here is walked by an RNG. But ONE LIST ORDER IS A POSITIONAL CONTRACT: `craft_focus` is exactly two distinct crafts, and derive._apply_rule() resolves a {'craft': N} derivation rule as traits['craft_focus'][rule['craft']]. derivation.json indexes 0 into culture.livelihood.primary and 1 into culture.livelihood.secondary, so SWAPPING THE TWO ENTRIES SWAPS A PEOPLE'S PRIMARY AND SECONDARY LIVELIHOOD. policy._check_axis() enforces exactly CRAFT_COUNT=2 distinct values but says nothing about which comes first.
The `races` and `peoples` mapping key order is FREE: both are keyed lookups, and heritage_identity() sorts the pairs it is given and serialises with sort_keys=True.

ABSENCE THAT IS NOT EMPTINESS: a civilization absent from `peoples` resolves to its parent race base -- that is the deliberate property that lets a new people arrive with a plausible culture and tongue already attached (derive._resolve, and a registry test that injects a synthetic entity depends on it). Absence means 'a plain member of the race', not 'no traits'. Within a delta, an axis that is absent is inherited, and an axis that RESTATES its inherited value RAISES -- merge_traits() rejects it, so a delta is the difference from the archetype and cannot be written out in full. A race base, by contrast, must name exactly all seventeen axes (lint_traits). `magic_school` is restricted to the eight KNOWN_SCHOOLS; naming one of the four hidden Outside schools (blood, void, rot, eldritch) raises with a specific message, because generation can never raise one.

The heritage identity hash does NOT cover these bytes. heritage.heritage_identity() (heritage/derive.py:330) hashes the RESOLVED peoples instead -- resolved = {cid: _resolve(cid, parent) for cid, parent in sorted(pairs)}, then sha256 of json.dumps(resolved, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')).encode('utf-8'). That is a THIRD serialisation scheme in this codebase, distinct from both of the two you already have: registry_identity() (icarus_sim/civilization_registry.py:308) uses ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':') and NO sort_keys, and castle_planner (icarus_sim/castle_planner.py:39) uses sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':') and the ensure_ascii=True default. heritage is sort_keys=True AND ensure_ascii=False, so it agrees with neither on a non-ASCII string. sort_keys sorts MAPPING keys only -- it does not touch list element order, so every list marked a contract below also moves this digest. For the twelve civilizations the registry ships, in terrain_civilizations.civilization_report's pair order (tuple((key, entity_rules(key)['parent_race_id']) for key in civilization_ids()), which heritage_identity then sorts), the expected value at FantasyWorldGenerator b67c99b is sha256=9b708d23e468beb4c3f775415405b5aa8991f21c7d402aa200cd6aa99a0b2189 with revision={traits:1, derivation:1, lexicon:1, overrides:1, appearance:1}. `source_sha256` in this file is a plain digest of the source file's raw bytes, recorded for provenance only; nothing in the Python computes it.

REVISION 2 (2026-09-23): the gnome's lifespan_tempo is `ancient`, to hold the owner's 750-year gnome inside the tempo's span.
source_note: Seventeen categorical key traits per people. Six soma axes drive phonology, three register axes drive prosody and script, eight social axes drive culture. No numbers live here: the quantitative habitat profile is civilizations.json and these must never restate it. Each race base is the unmarked member, so human_heartland, elf and dwarf carry empty deltas and every other entry reads as its diff from its archetype.
